versions.title_at_revision: Safe operation of integrated electrical power system
versions.text: Criterion: Verify that operation of the integrated electrical power system for normal and emergency modes is safe. This includes use of actual or simulated drives and loads, all flight and control configurations, transition between modes, bus switching, load shedding, fault condition operation (detection, clearing, and reconfiguration), and assurance that no single fault affects more than one power source. Standard: Proper function of electric power sources is maintained whether connected in combination or independently. No malfunction or failure of any electric power source or bus impairs the ability of any remaining source or bus to supply circuits essential for safe operation. Load management, fault detection/protection and bus switching arrangements maintain safe delivery of electric power. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, and inspection of documentation. Operation of the integrated system during normal and emergency modes is verified with analysis of the engineering design, Electrical Loads Analysis, and FMECA. Proper functioning of the integrated system is verified by system level tests including on-aircraft testing using documented test procedures for checkout. References: For guidance/principles regarding/affecting design and operation of safe integrated electrical systems: JSSG-2009: H.3.4.8, H.4.4.8, H.3.4.8.4, H.4.4.8.4, H.3.4.8.5, H.4.4.8.5 MIL-STD-464 MIL-E-7016 AFGS-87219 ADS-51-HDBK: Chapter/Section 8-7 14 CFR 23.1351-23.1367; 25.1351-25.1363

versions.title_at_revision: Safe operation of integrated electrical power system
versions.text:
Standard: For the air system, operation of the integrated EPS for normal and emergency modes operates IAW its designed states and modes. This includes use of actual or simulated drives and loads, all flight and control configurations, transition between modes, bus switching, load shedding, and fault condition operation (e.g., detection, clearing, and reconfiguration). No malfunction or failure of any electric power source, component, or bus impairs the ability of any remaining source or bus to supply power. The integrated EPS isolates fault conditions, localizing them to the lowest level protective device. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Failure conditions of electrical power sources are identified and analyzed in the FMECA to understand the impacts to the total EPS.
(2) Electrical power system analysis verifies the components of the EPS are appropriately specified for their intended operation, during all modes of operation, once integrated into the EPS. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Electrical system tests, using production or production representative power system components, verifies the operation of the integrated EPS during normal, transfer, abnormal, fault clearing, and emergency modes of operation.
  (2) Ground test: Air vehicle ground testing substantiates operation of the integrated EPS during normal, transfer, abnormal, and emergency modes of operation. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (3) Flight test: Air vehicle flight testing substantiates operation of the integrated EPS during normal, transfer, and emergency modes of operation.
